[JustWantToSave] Yep! I put my name down for one. Originally I thought it wouldn't fit my place, but it seems it could fit.
Beats out my tiny "portable" devanti washing machine that can hold a couple shirts and bed sheets at most.
[J5] Its a shame that lg washing machines suck balls
[JustWantToSave] I feel like if your budget is $250 for a washing machine, you wont get a better option new.
The people these are aimed at (like myself) would and are extremely grateful for this being an option at all.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] This has restored my faith in humanity. I find LG washing machines are great, especially the modern ones.
[carrawa] Price is great but replacing a top loader albeit new that can't or struggles to handle larger loads like doonas etc will end up being a problem e.g 350-400+ GSM quilts. A lot of people would need to do two loads instead of one depending on washing patterns and household size, or use an expensive laundromat. From experience with a 7.5kg front loader. I don't fault it other than size options.
Not to mention reliability of your existing unit / brand.
If they had a larger machine option for a graduating price in size, it would be interesting.
Those with back issues and bending down unless you can get it wall mounted might regret it. You have to lift from the ground too,not good for some. Stick to the top loader.
[BestTechAdvisor] Those with back issues and bending down unless you can get it wall mounted might regret it.
Good point, though you can get drawers and cupboards made to fit under front loaders for this reason. I'd suggest looking into this as an option since leaning over and into a top loader isn't optimal for those with bad backs either.
[tubeidea] The reliability is of particular concern. I've heard many stories of people who have issues with their machines that are only a few years old, they try to get them repaired only to find out that they aren't worth repairing, or aren't capable of being repaired, with the repairmen telling them that this is by design.
The buyitforlife subreddit is full of stories like that, older machines are recommended as they last decades and the few newer machines that are still somewhat good are usually in the process of being enshittified.
Old ones are not as energy efficient, but they're much more reliable on average, and probably more powerful.
[ribbon] What happen if the pensioner don’t have a top load machine ?
[toasty] They can pick one up for free at the closest location doing hard rubbish collection or on marketplace
[Surfer Dude] Arguably a top loader is easier to use for a pensioner than a front loader (assuming its not been lifted off the floor)
[TaurusHead] in a need of a washing machine but I don't qualify under any of those criteria
